Definition: from G5351; decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively):--corruption, destroy, perish.
BiblicalUsage: Phthora is decay, the ruin that eats away at what was made good. Paul says the whole creation waits to be delivered from the bondage of corruption in Romans 8:21, and that sowing to the flesh reaps corruption in Galatians 6:8. Our bodies are sown in corruption, says 1 Corinthians 15:42, but Peter promises an escape from the corruption in the world through lust in 2 Peter 1:4.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe decay is the signature of the fall on everything, and resurrection is God's answer to it. That is why I hold that the gospel is not a repair job but a rescue from corruption itself.
